current.text: Toronto swapped Brandon Ingram for Kawhi Leonard. Kawhi is the better player and uses more possessions than Ingram did.
Most experts doubt a big step forward this season, because Kawhi Leonard now takes usage that could have gone to Barnes.
He should not lose many touches next to Kawhi, because his value comes from facilitation rather than usage.
Experts place him around 12th to 17th overall in 9-cat. They call ESPN's rank of 10 too high, and one expert passed on him at pick 10.
An ADP in the 30s is too late for him.
He went for 35 USD in a mock auction. The expert expected a price above 30 USD and called 35 USD about right.
He is a projected starter with Quickley, Barrett, Leonard and Poeltl, and part of the expected closing five.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games. The roster is thin after a solid top seven.
The Raptors have 15 back-to-backs, three of them in the playoff weeks.

durable.text: He is one of the best help rim protectors in the league and anchors the Toronto defense.
His shooting is a question mark, and he makes few threes.
He fills many categories. He has guard-like assists for a forward or center, plus strong steals, blocks and rebounds.
Turnovers are his weak category for his position.
He is a second-round option next to Giannis in a punt FT% build.

note: Experts see him as a 12th to 17th overall pick in 9-cat, not a top 10 player. Plan around a price between our league's 31 USD from last season and the 35 USD mock result, and not the 42 to 55 USD site values. He fits punt TO builds and Giannis punt FT% builds best, because his assists, steals and blocks are rare for an F/C. Early in the season, check whether his assists and shot volume hold up next to Kawhi Leonard.
